_why:
Proves nextseek-aggregate live on Container-CC, which has never been observed. Metadata aggregation stays routed to NS (it answers correctly there, ~30 s, $0), so the case is FORCED onto CC; it cannot share a file with the routed probe because --force-route applies to every turn of a run.
  manage.py nessie --tier full --force-route cc --cases /app/NessieAI/tests/nessie_tests/probes/probe-2026-09-23-cc-aggregate-forced.json --out /app/runs/cc-aggregate-<date>
A forced run needs a superuser account (a non-admin's force is dropped silently; the harness preflight proves it landed). Route criteria are stripped from forced arms, so none is written here; cc_trace_text is engine-neutral and is scored.
_instance_warning: Measured on the workstation's graph on 2026-09-23. Re-pin with pin_probe_truths.py (mode 'each', four numbers).

cc_aggregate_forced.description: A metadata breakdown, forced onto Container-CC.

variants.name: Operator case b: Container-CC aggregates a metadata question NS answers today
variants._why: Run with --force-route cc: the router would send this to nextseek_query, which answers it. The point is that CC can aggregate too, through nextseek-aggregate (the trace must show it). IMPAcTb samples by Species: 83,582 have none; of those that do, Macaca fascicularis 327, Macaca mulatta (Rhesus) 239, Mus musculus 119, Rhesus macaque 88, then smaller spellings. The four largest are pinned.

turns.label: main
turns.query: What species are the samples in the IMPAcTb project, and how many of each?

ccagg.impactb_species_forced.cypher: MATCH (s:Sample)-[:IN_PROJECT]->(p:Project {title:'IMPAcTb'}) WITH DISTINCT s WHERE s.Species IS NOT NULL RETURN s.Species AS species, count(*) AS n ORDER BY n DESC LIMIT 4
